measurements.evidence_quote: The charge density significantly drops with the pH decrease (the zeta potential of PET particles varies from -34.5 to -9.5, at pH 7.0 and 3.0, respectively) due to the protonation of carboxylic groups. || A Zetasizer NanoZS from Malvern Instruments was used to measure the zeta potential of the cationic cellulose polymer in solution and PET MPs in two different pHs (pH 7.0 and 3.0). || The zeta potential was measured at 25 °C with an equilibration time of 60 s.

The charge density significantly drops with the pH decrease (the zeta potential of PET particles varies from -34.5 to -9.5, at pH 7.0 and 3.0, respectively) due to the protonation of carboxylic groups. || A Zetasizer NanoZS from Malvern Instruments was used to measure the zeta potential of the cationic cellulose polymer in solution and PET MPs in two different pHs (pH 7.0 and 3.0). || The zeta potential was measured at 25 °C with an equilibration time of 60 s.

This explains the low zeta potential observed for “model” MP suspensions at neutral to alkaline pH, ca. -12 mV, as the presence of carboxylic groups is quite low and was not observed in NMR experiments (below the detection/quantification limit of NMR).
The NMR results are well aligned with the zeta potential values of PET MP pellets, which presented a value of ca. -45 mV at neutral pH.
